Great. Below is a comprehensive 12-week conditioning program designed for a 58-year-old male, six months post-MI, cleared for Phase II cardiac rehab. The plan emphasizes safe progression, heart-rate targets (under ~70% of age-predicted max, ~115 bpm for this client), avoidance of Valsalva, and non-maximal effort lifting. It’s structured to be performed in a full gym and includes weekly progression, exercise selections, sets/reps, intensity cues, HR/prescription guidance, warm-up/cool-down, and basic nutrition/recovery considerations. Please customize based on the client’s actual medical clearance, medications (e.g., beta-blockers) which may blunt HR response, and individual responses.

Assumptions and safety notes
- Target HR: keep in zone with HR_rest + 20–30 bpm for most sessions, or HR not to exceed 115 bpm if age-predicted max rule is prioritized. If on beta-blockers, use RPE rather than HR for effort (light = 9–11, somewhat hard = 12–13, hard = 14–15 on 6–20 Borg scale).
- Valsalva avoided. Exhale through exertion, intra-abdominal pressure minimized; DB/gym machine safe.
- No lifting to failure. RPE monitoring; technique first.
- Medical clearance stable; monitor for warning signs (angina, dizziness, excessive shortness, palpitations). Adjust as needed.

Program overview
- Duration: 12 weeks
- Frequency: 4 sessions per week (2 upper-lower split) with optional active recovery days
- Structure: Progressive overload via volume, some intensity, technique focus, and conditioning work
- Conditioning modalities: steady-state cardio, interval work with low-to-moderate intensity, and functional resistance circuits
- Recovery: mobility, soft-tissue work, sleep emphasis, nutrition basics
- Nutrition guidance: support for energy needs, heart-healthy focus, modest caloric balance if weight management is desired; stay hydrated; consider timing around workouts.

Week-by-week plan (weeks 1–4: foundation; weeks 5–8: progressive overload; weeks 9–12: consolidation and maintenance with higher conditioning)

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 — Foundation and safety acclimation
Goals: re-establish movement patterns, build base aerobic capacity, establish HR/RPE benchmarks, reinforce technique.

Weekly structure (4 days)
- Day 1: Upper body cardio-based + light resistance
- Day 2: Lower body cardio-based + light resistance
- Day 3: Full-body mobility, core, and light resistance
- Day 4: Cardio conditioning + light full-body circuits

Common warm-up (all sessions)
- 5–8 minutes treadmill incline walk or bike at light pace
- Dynamic mobility: arm circles, leg swings, hip circles, thoracic rotations (2 rounds)
- Light activation: glute bridges, banded lateral walks, scapular push-ups (1 set of 10–15 reps each)

Safety cues
- HR: aim for 60–70% of age-pred max or RPE 11–12 (1–10 scale) under beta-blockers. If HR too high or symptomatic, reduce pace.
- Movement: 2–3 sets of 10–12 reps for accessory lifts; emphasize technique.

Week 1
- Day 1 – Upper body cardio + resistance
  - Cardio: 10 minutes steady-state on bike or elliptical (RPE 11–12)
  - Strength (2 sets each, 12–15 reps, controlled tempo 2–0-2)
    - Dumbbell bench press
    - Seated cable row
    - Dumbbell shoulder press (neutral grip)
    - Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up
  - Core: 2 x 12 curl-to-press or anti-extension holds (plank 20–30s)

- Day 2 – Lower body cardio + resistance
  - Cardio: 10 minutes incline treadmill walk: 3–4% incline, 1.5–2.5 mph; RPE 11
  - Strength (2 sets, 12–15 reps)
    - Goblet squat or leg press (light)
    - Leg extension (light)
    - Hamstring curl
    - Hip adductor/abductor machine
  - Core: standing anti-rotational Pallof press 2 x 12

- Day 3 – Full body mobility + core
  - Mobility flow: 15 minutes (hips, thoracic spine, shoulders)
  - Circuit (2 rounds, 12 reps each, light dumbbells)
    - Dumbbell chest fly (light)
    - Seated row or resistance band row
    - Dumbbell Romanian deadlift (light)
    - Step-ups (lower height)
  - Core: dead bug variations 2 x 12 per side

- Day 4 – Cardio conditioning & light circuit
  - Cardio: 12 minutes continuous cycling, HR ~110–115 bpm or RPE 11–12
  - Circuit (2 rounds, 12 reps each, 30–45s rest)
    - Push-ups (incline if needed)
    - Dumbbell goblet squat
    - Seated leg extension (light)
    - Standing cable push/pull
  - Flexibility: 5–10 minutes static stretches

Week 2
- Similar structure; increase volume slightly
- All 2x12–15 reps; add 1 extra set for main lifts (total 3 sets)
- Cardio: add 2 minutes to steady-state segments; maintain HR cap

Week 3
- Progression: add a small amount of resistance (increase weight by 2–5% if technique solid)
- Keep reps 10–12 for main lifts to maintain form; consider 3 sets
- Cardio: 14 minutes steady-state, maintain HR target

Week 4
- Deload style: reduce weight slightly if fatigue; maintain technique
- Keep 3 sets on resistance; reps 8–12 on main lifts, 12–15 accessory
- Cardio: 15–18 minutes steady-state; optional light intervals (30s light/90s easy) twice per week if HR and symptoms are controlled

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 — Progressive overload and interval conditioning
Goals: increase muscular endurance and aerobic capacity while staying within HR/RPE limits.

Weekly structure (4 days)
- Day 1: Upper body strength + cardio mix
- Day 2: Lower body strength + interval cardio
- Day 3: Full body circuit with greater emphasis on conditioning
- Day 4: Active recovery + mobility

Week 5
- Day 1 – Upper body strength
  - Warm-up
  - Main lifts (3 sets x 10–12 reps)
    - Dumbbell incline bench press
    - Seated cable row
    - Overhead press with dumbbells (neutral grip)
    - Face pulls
  - Accessory: triceps pushdown 2 x 12, biceps curls 2 x 12
  - Cardio: 8–10 minutes on bike, steady-state (RPE 11–12)

- Day 2 – Lower body strength + intervals
  - Squats: Goblet or barbell squat (3 x 12)
  - Leg press or hack squat: 3 x 12
  - Romanian deadlift: 3 x 12
  - Calf raise: 3 x 15
  - Cardio intervals: 6 rounds x 30s hard/90s easy on bike or treadmill; keep around RPE 13–14 during work interval; ensure HR under 115

- Day 3 – Full body conditioning circuit
  - 3 rounds, 10–12 reps each, minimal rest
    - Dumbbell row
    - Dumbbell squat to press
    - Walking lunges (bodyweight or light dumbbells)
    - Assisted pull-downs
    - Plank variations (20–40s)

- Day 4 – Active recovery
  - Light cardio (20–30 minutes) at brisk walk or easy cycle
  - Mobility: 15 minutes focusing on hips, thoracic spine
  - Breathing/relaxation: 5–10 minutes

Week 6

- Main lifts: 3 sets x 8–12 reps
- Cardio: intervals extended to 8 rounds x 30s work/60s rest; maintain HR target
- Include brief tempo cues: 2–0-2 for control

Week 7
- Similar to Week 6 but add 1–2 extra reps if form stable
- Cardio: longer steady-state 12–15 minutes on one day

Week 8
- Progression: push closer to 10–12 reps with modest weight increase
- Cardio intervals: 8–10 rounds; ensure adequate recovery
- Deload concepts: if fatigue accrues, reduce volume by 1 set per exercise

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 — Consolidation and conditioning emphasis
Goals: maximize conditioning while maintaining safety, refine technique, prepare for transition to general fitness.

Weekly structure (4 days)
- Day 1: Upper push/pull with cardio emphasis
- Day 2: Lower body strength + power-ish tempo
- Day 3: Full-body conditioning circuit (shorter rest)
- Day 4: Long steady-state cardio + mobility

Week 9
- Upper body
  - Chest press machine or dumbbell bench press: 3 x 8–10
  - Seated row: 3 x 8–10
  - Dumbbell incline press: 3 x 8–10
  - Lat pulldown: 3 x 10
  - Core: Pallof press 3 x 12 per side
  - Cardio: 12–15 minutes steady-state

Week 10
- Lower body
  - Front squats or goblet squats: 3 x 8–10
  - Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8–10
  - Leg press: 3 x 10
  - Hamstring curl: 3 x 12
  - Calf raises: 3 x 12
  - Cardio: intervals 6 rounds x 30s work/60s rest

Week 11
- Full-body conditioning focus
  - Circuit: 4 rounds, 8–12 reps
    - Push-ups (modify as needed)
    - Rowing ergometer or machine row
    - DB step-up to overhead press
    - Cable pull-through or hip hinge
    - Plank 30–40s
  - Cardio: 15–20 minutes steady-state or interval mix

Week 12
- Progression consolidation
  - Repeat Week 11 structure but aim for increased reps by 1–2 or slightly heavier load
  - Cardio: 20–25 minutes steady-state, or 8–10 rounds x 30s work/60s rest if tolerated
  - Focus on technique and breathing control

Recurring session structure details
- Reps and sets
  - Foundation weeks: 2–3 sets of 12–15 reps for most exercises
  - Progressive weeks: 3 sets of 8–12 reps for main compounds; accessory lifts 2–3 sets of 10–15 reps
  - Never 1RM-oriented; avoid max effort
- Tempo
  - Emphasize controlled lifting: 2 seconds concentric, 2 seconds eccentric (2-0-2)
  - On high-safety lifts, use slower eccentrics to reduce injury risk
- Rest
  - Between sets: 60–90 seconds for larger lifts; 45–60 seconds for accessories
  - Between circuits: 2–3 minutes if needed for safety

Exercise selection notes
- Upper body
  - Pressing: DB incline press, machine chest press, push-ups (inclined if needed)
  - Pulling: Seated row, cable row, lat pulldown, assisted pull-ups
  - Shoulders: Dumbbell or machine lateral raises; avoid heavy overhead strain
  - Trunk: Pallof press, anti-rotation exercises

- Lower body

Here is a cohesive, 12-week conditioning program that combines the Phase II base (Weeks 5–8 style) for safety regression when needed, with the Phase III progression for weeks where clearance allows. It maintains a 4-day weekly structure (two upper–lower splits) plus an integrated light-strength block, and adds a clear plan for when to revert to Phase II and how to re-introduce Phase III intervals if/when re-cleared. The plan emphasizes safety, HR/RPE guidance, and non–maximal loading, suitable for a 58-year-old male, ~6 months post-MI, with the cardiologist approving phases as described.

Assumptions and safety notes
- Primary targets:
  - Phase II cardio: HR under approx 70% age-pred max or RPE 11–12 (light–moderate); beta-blocker patients: rely on RPE/conversation pace.
  - Phase III cardio (when cleared): HR cap up to 85% age-pred max or RPE 12–14; still no max effort lifting; Valsalva minimized.
- Lifting: no max lifts; technique over load; avoid Valsalva; progressive overload only when form is solid and symptoms are absent.
- Symptoms to watch: chest pain, dizziness, excessive dyspnea, nausea, palpitations, or unusual fatigue. Stop and consult clinician as needed.
- Medication considerations: HR targets may be blunted by beta-blockers; use RPE and conversation pace as primary metrics.

Weekly structure
- 4 sessions per week
  - Day 1: Upper body cardio-based + light resistance
  - Day 2: Lower body cardio-based + light resistance
  - Day 3: Full-body mobility, core, light resistance
  - Day 4: Cardio conditioning or interval conditioning (adjusted by phase and safety)

- Optional light-strength block: Weeks 1–4 and continued as a parallel safety layer

Phase I foundation and safety acclimation (Weeks 1–4)
- Purpose: re-establish movement patterns, posture, and low-demand aerobic base; build RPE familiarity; practice breathing and Valsalva-free technique.
- Cardio: 8–12 minutes continuous at low-to-moderate intensity; progress to 16–22 minutes by Week 4 if symptom-free.
- Strength (2–3 sets, 12–15 reps, tempo 2-0-2)
  - Upper: Dumbbell bench press or machine chest press; Seated cable row; Dumbbell shoulder press (neutral); Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up
  - Lower: Goblet squat (light); Leg extension (light); Hamstring curl (light); Hip adductor/abductor
  - Core: Pallof press 2 x 12 per side; Dead bug 2 x 12 per side
- Light strength integration: add 1 extra set to main lifts on Week 3–4 if technique solid

Phase II progression (Weeks 5–8) — strength foundations with conditioning base
- Structure: 4 days with an emphasis on technique, muscular endurance, and steady-state cardio
- Cardio prescription: 70% max HR cap or RPE 11–12; 12–22 minutes continuous; basic progression by week
- Strength prescription (3 sets x 10–12 reps for main lifts; 2–3 sets for accessories)
  - Upper: Incline press or DB press; Seated row; Overhead press (neutral); Lat pulldown
